Document evidence and qualityApplied guidance2026-09-07

Make document quality review evidence-backed

Use the Site for reusable methods and a source-grounded brief for each application. Treat integrity, chronology, and extraction as prerequisites to judging reader and document quality.

DecisionExpand the existing editorial skills, reconcile Leah and Sofia, use a small content trial, and require version-specific independent findings before a review can pass.
EvidenceA resume audit found changed attribution and action verbs, weakened context, cosmetic variations, and approval labels without inspectable review evidence. The process is adopted; its effect on the next resume remains untested.
AlternativesAnother full visual redesign; a universal resume score; additional personas; an app-managed runtime. Start with existing capabilities and a bounded trial.
TradeoffsClaim tracking and concrete findings take more care. Focus them on consequential claims and affected checks; do not add a general approval ritual to every edit.
AffectsSkills, Leah, Sofia, job-search handoffs, and Docs. Trial procedure remains isolated.
Revisit whenA real trial still produces generic or misleading content, the reviewer cannot find evidence, or the process creates effort without improving the reader’s understanding.
DEC-001AppliedInformation architecture

Flow hierarchy for persona work

Organize each person’s work into foundational, supporting, and edge-case flows, with the activity inventory embedded inside each flow.

QuestionShould the persona page follow a day, a list of activities, or the outcomes the person is trying to produce?
DecisionUse flow hierarchy as the primary structure. Each tier can contain multiple workflows.
RationaleThis keeps cadence, tools, priorities, friction, and recovery work attached to the context where they matter.
AffectsPersona cards, persona detail views, and the persona-research guidance.
EvidenceLayout Lab prototype · Current Docs guidance
Revisit whenReal persona research shows that users need a different first-order way to compare work.
DEC-002AppliedSkill presentation

Skill index plus deep dive

Keep the complete capability set visible, then select one skill to inspect its triggers, operating model, quality signals, workflows, and evidence.

QuestionCan someone see all the capabilities and still understand one skill deeply?
DecisionUse a scan-friendly skill index with a focused deep-dive panel.
RationaleThe index supports orientation; depth belongs in the selected skill instead of a wall of content.
AffectsPersona detail pages, the Skills space, and the $persona-skills guidance.
EvidenceSkill Layout Lab prototype · Current Docs guidance
Revisit whenSkill reuse or relationship density makes the index difficult to scan or the panel too shallow.
DEC-003ParkedExploration

Full skill network map

Show multi-hop relationships between primitive capabilities, composed skills, workflows, and personas.

DecisionPark until the focused skill map needs a global relationship view.
Why parkedA global graph needs filtering, navigation, and accessible list-view rules before it becomes useful.
NotesConsider neighborhood depth, relationship filters, and keyboard-friendly alternatives.
DEC-004ParkedAuthoring

Skill composition editor

Let a maintainer assemble composed skills from existing primitives and connect them with typed relationships.

DecisionPark until relationship editing has stronger validation, permissions, and versioning.
Why parkedEditing shared relationships safely has a larger integrity and governance surface than the static library needs today.
NotesStart with reuse suggestions, duplicate and cycle checks, and an explicit rationale for every new connection.
DEC-005ParkedAssessment

Skill coverage and assessment

Show which skills are well evidenced, thinly evidenced, or missing across personas and workflows.

DecisionPark until more personas and skill applications have been researched consistently.
Why parkedCoverage metrics would create false precision before the evidence model is mature enough.
NotesPotential views include evidence confidence, workflow coverage, proficiency signals, and validation gaps.
DEC-006ParkedImpact

Dependency-aware version history

Show what downstream personas, workflows, and composed skills are affected when a reusable capability changes.

DecisionPark until the relationship graph has enough real reuse to create meaningful change impact.
Why parkedImpact views are most useful when a change can affect several real dependents.
NotesPair relationship diffs with reconciliation prompts and a review queue before changes propagate.
DEC-007AppliedInformation architecture2026-09-10

Operating Packs are contextual library space

Catalog reusable, file-based operating context alongside the existing library spaces while keeping actual Markdown source outside the catalog when appropriate.

QuestionWhere should domain or project instructions, standards, conventions, procedures, references, and validation guidance live when they are reusable but not executable capabilities?
DecisionAdd Operating Packs as a first-class space with a small source/location record, explicit availability, and scoped Persona, Skill, workflow, Playbook, and Tool-use relationships.
RationaleContextual rules need a durable home that does not turn Skills into project instruction or Playbooks into duplicated policy. Scoped applications keep a pack relevant to the work where it applies.
TradeoffsThe catalog does not transport or execute packs, and external references may remain planned or unavailable until verified. Project conventions remain local unless later evidence supports broader reuse.
AffectsOrientation routing, Docs, Site navigation, the Operating Pack catalog, lifecycle Skills, and reconciliation guidance. Existing Persona, Skill, Tool, and Playbook definitions remain separate.
Revisit whenA pack needs executable runtime behavior, repeated rules reveal a generalizable Skill, a Playbook duplicates pack content, or external source transport becomes a separately authorized product need.
